Joe — great meeting yesterday. As a follow-up, I want to capture the intended flow for operator access and our fallback options so we have a clear playbook for the cutover test. High level: 

- Primary auth: SAML SSO via Finova IdP -> Assertion mapped to Redwood operator role (role mapping lives in private control plane).
- Provisioning: SCIM push will populate user accounts and group memberships into the private control plane directory; service accounts for automated operator tooling can be created by SCIM if Finova prefers auto-provisioning.
- Fallback: If SAML assertion validation fails, we allow a short-lived, auditable emergency token flow that requires approval from two on-call operators; tokens are single-use and expire in 15 minutes.

Before the playtest we need:
- Finova to confirm SCIM attribute mapping for the operator role (email, employeeNumber, groups).
- A signed-off emergency operator contact list (names + mobile).

Joe — quick answers inline: 

On SCIM provisioning:
- We can accept "operatorGroup" as a group attribute and will map it into the control plane as a group with the tag "operator:external".
- externalId will be honored; if present we will create a service account record using that externalId and store the mapping in the audit log. If externalId is missing we will fallback to generating a UUID and include the sourceId in the user metadata.

On SAML fallback:
- If SAML assertion validation fails due to signature/time skew we will not silently allow access. The emergency token flow Rishi mentioned requires two approvals via the private control plane UI / API. We will surface the assertion failure reason in the audit event but redact any PII.

Attachments: I pushed a short SAML assertion mapping guide and the initial operator access matrix to the shared Drive.
